explanation: Format n as a zero-padded 32-character binary string, reverse those characters, and parse the reversed string in base two. The unsigned 32-bit bound ensures formatting produces exactly 32 characters.
timeComplexity: O(32)=O(1): formatting, reversing, and parsing each process exactly 32 binary digits.
spaceComplexity: O(32)=O(1) auxiliary space for the formatted and reversed 32-character strings.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The format includes all 32 bit positions, including leading zeros. Reversal maps original bit i to position 31-i; base-two parsing assigns exactly the numerical weight of each reversed position. Thus the returned nonnegative integer is the required fixed-width reversal.
walkthrough: For n=3, formatting yields thirty zeros followed by 11. Reversal yields 11 followed by thirty zeros, so parsing returns 2^31+2^30=3221225472.
edgeCases: Exactly 32 bits are reversed, not all 64 bits of the carrier type.
The result is nonnegative in the range 0..2^32-1.
